name: Shashai
overview: Shashai is a male figure mentioned in the book of Ezra as a descendant of Bani. His notable distinction is that he had married a foreign wife, an issue addressed in the post-exilic community as recorded in Ezra 10:40. Other details such as his tribe or additional background are not provided in Scripture.
namesAndTitles: The name Shashai is a proper name meaning 'noble.' This name is not indicated as being given by God, but it reflects a characteristic of dignity or honor as understood in the Hebrew context.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly identifies Shashai as a descendant of Bani. Beyond this lineage, no further family relationships are recorded in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Shashai's significance lies in his inclusion in the list of those who had married foreign wives, highlighting the challenges faced by the returned exiles in maintaining covenant purity. His mention underscores the community's efforts to restore faithfulness to God's commands after the exile. Through Shashai, the narrative illustrates the broader theme of repentance and renewal within Israel during this period.
